description: Given a list of integers arr sorted in non-decreasing order and an integer target, return the index of the first occurrence of target in arr, or -1 if target does not occur. A non-negative result must be a valid index whose element equals target, with no earlier element equal to target; a result of -1 means that no element equals target. The input list is not modified.
notes: VERINA reads the output index with Lean's arr[i]!, which yields 0 for an out-of-range index. Both specs instead require a non-negative result to be a valid index (result < length), so they reject only the degenerate outputs that VERINA accepts through that default value (an out-of-range index when the searched value is 0). As in VERINA, negative results other than -1 are not constrained.
